rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed yet, so the most critical need is to establish a performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the design space: it uses the most standard and computationally cheap encoder (PCA), the simplest profile setting (single), and no image modality. This experiment will (1) provide a reference accuracy/F1 against which all subsequent unimodal and multimodal configurations can be compared, (2) reveal how well RNA data alone performs, which is essential for determining whether image or multimodal fusion adds value, and (3) reduce uncertainty about the overall difficulty of the classification task. Under a limited budget, starting with the simplest baseline is the highest-information first step because every subsequent experiment's value is interpreted relative to this reference point.

Evidence: Only one experiment (config_001, rna_only/pca_n2000/singleprofile) has been completed, yielding a low accuracy of 0.485 and F1 of 0.464, indicating the task is challenging and the current RNA representation captures limited signal. Uncertainty: The most fundamental unknown is whether the image modality carries useful discriminative signal for this task. Without knowing this, it is impossible to prioritize among the many multimodal configurations or to decide whether to invest in better RNA encoders. What this tests: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_001, isolating the effect of modality while holding profile_setting constant. Why it is the best use of the next budget: If image accuracy substantially exceeds 0.485, it justifies prioritizing multimodal configurations and stronger image encoders (ViT-L). If it is comparable or lower, it confirms RNA is the stronger (or equally weak) modality and shifts focus to better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) or multiprofile aggregation. Either outcome dramatically narrows the search space for all subsequent experiments, making this the highest-information experiment available.

Evidence: RNA-only (pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieves 48.5% acc while image-only (resnet50, singleprofile) is very weak at 20.8%, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We have only one RNA data point and don't know whether multiprofile aggregation (vs singleprofile) meaningfully improves the RNA signal. This experiment (config_002) tests multiprofile + avgpool with the same pca_n2000 encoder, providing the cleanest isolated comparison to config_001 by changing only the profile setting and adding a simple aggregation. It is the best use of the next budget slot because: (1) it directly extends our strongest configuration, (2) it resolves whether the profile/aggregation axis matters for the dominant modality before we invest in more complex encoders or multimodal fusion, and (3) the result will inform whether multiprofile is worth pursuing in any multimodal setup, reducing uncertainty across a large portion of the remaining search space.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a strong +10.6% gain over the singleprofile baseline (config_001, 0.485), confirming multiprofile aggregation is the most impactful design choice so far. However, we have only tested one aggregation method (avgpool). Uncertainty: it is unknown whether transformer aggregation would further improve multiprofile performance or whether avgpool is already near-optimal for this encoder. This experiment (config_003) provides a clean, single-variable comparison against config_002 (only aggregation changes: transformer vs avgpool), isolating the effect of aggregation architecture. Why it is the best next step: (1) it directly extends our best-performing configuration with a logical, minimal change; (2) the result will tell us whether to invest subsequent budget in transformer-based pipelines (which would also benefit multimodal fusion experiments) or whether avgpool is sufficient and we should pivot to testing RNA encoder quality (scvi, scgpt); (3) it is the highest-information experiment per unit budget because a clear win/loss here partitions the remaining search space into two very different strategies.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA n2000, avgpool) is the best result so far at 0.591 acc, showing that multi-profile + avgpool is a strong aggregation strategy. Image-only is very weak (0.208), suggesting the RNA modality carries most of the signal. The key untested variable within the best-known RNA pipeline is the encoder: PCA n2000 is a simple linear projection, while scvi_n200 is a learned nonlinear variational representation. Question: Does a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) improve over PCA n2000 when paired with the best-known multi-profile + avgpool aggregation? Why this is the best next experiment: It isolates a single high-impact design choice (RNA encoder) while holding the proven-best settings fixed, giving a clean comparison. If scvi_n200 helps, it opens the door to scgpt and multimodal variants with learned encoders; if it does not, it confirms PCA is sufficient and redirects budget toward the multimodal or image-encoder questions. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: RNA dominates (0.485–0.650) while image-only is weak (0.208). Within RNA, we know scvi_n200 > pca_n2000 (0.650 vs 0.591) and avgpool > transformer (0.591 vs 0.519), both under multiprofile. The key remaining uncertainty among RNA encoders is where scgpt falls relative to scvi_n200. Question tested: config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) holds profile and aggregation fixed at their best-known settings, isolating the encoder variable for a clean three-way comparison (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200 vs scgpt). Why this is the best next experiment: RNA is the dominant signal source, so the encoder choice is the highest-leverage design decision. Resolving whether scgpt beats, matches, or trails scvi_n200 under identical conditions will either (a) confirm scvi_n200 as the optimal RNA backbone, letting us confidently move to multimodal fusion tests, or (b) reveal a superior encoder that reshapes the entire search. This is a low-variance, high-information experiment that reduces uncertainty on the most impactful axis before committing budget to the larger multimodal configuration space.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200, multiprofile, and avgpool (config_005) is the clear best at 0.650 acc, while image-only (config_010) is very weak at 0.208. This creates a critical uncertainty: does adding image features to the strong RNA signal provide complementary information, or does the weak image branch dilute performance? This is the single most consequential design decision for the remaining search. Config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the natural extension of the best RNA configuration into the multimodal setting, using the simpler concat fusion to minimize confounding variables. If it matches or beats 0.650, multimodal is a promising direction worth further exploration; if it underperforms, we can confidently rule out the large multimodal sub-space and concentrate budget on RNA-only refinements (e.g., scvi_n200 + transformer in config_006, or other RNA improvements). Resolving this question maximally reduces uncertainty about which branch of the search tree to pursue, making it the highest-information-value experiment under a limited budget.

The best result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 acc. We know avgpool outperformed transformer for pca_n2000 (0.591 vs 0.519), but scvi_n200 produces learned nonlinear embeddings where attention-based aggregation might better capture inter-profile relationships. Config_006 is a clean single-variable extension of our best result (changing only aggregation from avgpool to transformer). If transformer helps, it reveals an encoder-aggregation interaction and raises the ceiling for all future multimodal experiments. If it doesn't, we confirm avgpool is optimal for scvi_n200 and can redirect effort toward fusion strategy or stronger image encoders. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step: it directly probes the most promising configuration space around our current best with a well-motivated hypothesis.

Evidence: scvi_n200 + multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest RNA-only setup (0.650-0.653). The only multimodal test (config_030, resnet50, concat) scored 0.632, slightly *below* the RNA-only baseline (0.650), and image-only with resnet50 was very poor (0.208). This raises a critical uncertainty: is the image modality fundamentally unhelpful, or was resnet50 simply too weak an encoder to contribute useful signal? Question: config_036 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) isolates the image-encoder variable by swapping resnet50 → ViT-L while holding all other settings identical to config_030. If ViT-L multimodal exceeds the RNA-only baseline, it confirms the image modality is useful and justifies further multimodal exploration (fusion strategy, transformer aggregation). If it still underperforms RNA-only, it strongly indicates images are not contributing and remaining budget should focus on RNA-only refinements. This is the highest-information experiment under the limited budget because the answer directly determines the direction of all subsequent experiments.

The current best configuration (config_036, acc=0.7150) uses concat fusion to combine scvi_n200 RNA features with imagenet_vit_l image features. The fusion mechanism (concat vs weighted) has not been tested in any completed experiment, making it a major source of uncertainty. config_037 is a clean single-variable change from config_036 (only fusion: concat→weighted), allowing us to directly assess whether weighted fusion captures complementary modality information more effectively than simple concatenation. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it exploits the strongest evidence (best RNA encoder, best image encoder, multiprofile, avgpool) while probing the one untested design axis at the top of the performance landscape; (2) if weighted fusion helps, it opens a clear path to further gains; if it does not, we can confidently lock in concat and redirect budget toward aggregation (transformer) or other refinements. Under a limited budget, isolating one variable at the current optimum is the most efficient way to reduce uncertainty.
